what.title: What this is
what.body: Breadcrumb is a learning companion. You talk to an AI about what you want to learn, and alongside that it builds a map of what you have covered — no note-taking, no checking in.
what.point1: Concepts you talk about appear on the map by themselves, and fade where you have not been for a while.
what.point2: It suggests what you could look at next, based on what you already know. You are free to ignore it.
what.point3: Everything stays on this computer. No leaderboards, no streaks, no progress bars.

connect.title: Connect an AI service
connect.body: The app has no AI of its own. You bring an account from an AI service — any OpenAI-compatible one works. Fill in the address, the key and the model name.
connect.help: No account yet? Services like DeepSeek, Qwen and OpenAI all give you a key after signing up; paste it above. The key stays on this computer.
connect.notYetSaved: Not saved yet. Chat will not work without it, but you can skip and come back to settings whenever you like.

terms.title: Two things before you start
terms.privacy: What you write stays on your own computer. Nothing goes anywhere except the messages you send to the AI service above — no account, no cloud sync, no usage reporting.
terms.cost: You are spending on your own AI service account; this app neither charges you nor handles the money. Settings → Switches and spending tells you roughly what each feature costs per use, before you turn it on.
terms.switches: Every feature that costs money can be switched off on its own. There is also one switch for the internet: turn it off and everything that needs a connection stops, while the local parts carry on.
